purpose: One authoritative, living catalogue and taxonomy of every third-party provider, API, connector, Marketplace service, and external-execution platform Paige may use. This is a product-governance and delivery record. It does NOT install providers, hold credentials, call external APIs, create OAuth clients, create billing commitments, or ship provider functionality. v1.1 adds the API Expense & Operations Layer (per-provider operating cost + ownership visibility) — see expense_and_operations_schema and cost_tracks.
cardinal_rule: Listing a provider here NEVER means it is connected, available, or autonomous. A registry entry is a governance declaration, not a live capability. Connection is a per-tenant authorization fact; availability is a getTierFeatureSet()/RLS fact; autonomy is a resolve_tool_autonomy()/Trust-Compass fact. This document decides none of them (see rules R1 and R8).

status_vocabulary.LIVE: The integration is delivered and proven usable in the platform for its declared authority lane. A LIVE status is the integration's DELIVERY state, never a claim that any given tenant has connected it or that Paige may act autonomously on it.
status_vocabulary.PARTIAL: Some of the integration is real; the exact remaining gap is named in the entry.
status_vocabulary.PROPOSED: An approved or drafted DIRECTION exists; nothing is built. A design, handler stub, or plan does not make it more than PROPOSED.
status_vocabulary.UNAVAILABLE: The required contract/substrate does not exist yet, or the provider is not wired at all.
status_vocabulary.DEFERRED: Deliberately sequenced for a later slice; a decision to wait, not an absence of plan.
status_vocabulary.PROOF_OWED: Implemented and reachable in code, but authenticated end-to-end runtime proof (§32.c) is absent. Never report as LIVE.

authority_lanes.read: What Paige may safely read and understand (enumerated safe facts; never raw payload/secrets/credentials).
authority_lanes.draft: What she may draft/model/organize/recommend — a proposal with NO side effect.
authority_lanes.auto: What she may execute autonomously within a tenant-approved standing policy (§16 auto / §67 per-process grant). Consequential auto declares scope/caps/window, never a blanket ban.
authority_lanes.confirm: What requires owner confirmation before execution (§16 confirm, via paige_pending_confirmations). The escalation lane, not a default prohibition.
authority_lanes.prohibited: Permanently isolated/prohibited — raw secrets, credentials, unreviewed files, authority escalation, §38 merchant-of-record / holding tenant funds, §53 platform-tier escalation, or acts forbidden by law/provider.

cost_tracks.note: TWO distinct cost tracks. 'M1' unqualified is PROHIBITED (owner ruling 2026-09-06) — every m1_dependency and expense_and_operations.money_movement names which track applies. Provider API fees (operating cost) are treated separately from customer money movement (§38): Paige is never merchant of record and never silently charges a tenant's provider account.
cost_tracks.llm_cost_metering: Internal LLM-cost metering — platform operating-cost VISIBILITY for model (token) usage (paige_llm_trace -> platform_metered_events; autonomy-architecture §8.4). Observability of internal model cost. It is NOT authority to spend external money and NEVER satisfies a real-money spend dependency.
cost_tracks.m1_real_money_spend_control: M1 real-money spend control — the owner-priority backbone governing EXTERNAL provider spend: currency-aware caps, atomic reserve/adjust/release, provider-confirmed actuals, reconciliation, complete receipts, and Rail evidence (RE-2 M1-a/M1-b substrate; autonomy-architecture §10). REQUIRED for any provider that can create purchases, payments, ad spend, bookkeeping effects, financial obligations, or other real external spend. NEVER satisfied by LLM-token metering or estimated cost tracking. (M1-a = real-money reserve/confirm/reconcile actuals; M1-b = campaign/client-engagement scope caps.)
cost_tracks.none: No external provider spend and no billable model usage attributable to this provider action (e.g. a read-only data pull, telemetry, or a governance chokepoint). Operating API fees that are merely the cost of a normal read are visibility-only via the expense layer, not a real-money spend-control act.

tiers.note: Tier eligibility here is a GOVERNANCE DECLARATION of who the integration is FOR. Actual runtime availability is enforced by src/lib/tier/tierFeatures.ts (getTierFeatureSet/hasFeature, §60) and RLS — never by this document (§65 the name is not the authority). Values: eligible | ineligible | resell | deferred | na. Default distribution follows tier-matrix §61 unless an owner exception is recorded.
tiers.platform: God / Super Admin — the platform operator (us).
tiers.solo: Standalone Solo tenant, and Sub-account (same base feature set, §60). The only live tenant scope today.
tiers.agency_future: Agency tier — future; per §61 default an agency RESELLS most capabilities to sub-accounts rather than operator-using them.
tiers.enterprise_future: Enterprise tier — future; hybrid (Solo-union + Agency resell), per §61.

rules.rule: Listed is not connected/available/autonomous. No integration may be described as connected, available, or autonomous merely because it appears in this registry (the cardinal rule).

Honest status only. Record the true DELIVERY state from the six-word vocabulary. A design/handler/prototype/plan never raises an entry above PROPOSED; code without authenticated runtime proof is PROOF_OWED, never LIVE (§13/§32).

No secrets. NAMES, IDs, scopes and behaviour only — never a credential value, token, raw provider payload, or internal SID. Credential wiring lives in config-registry.md (names only) and in Supabase/Vercel secrets.

Platform Marketplace entries are GLOBAL CAPABILITY METADATA ONLY (marketplace_items: slug/type/name/category/pricing_model/metadata/global aggregates). They must NEVER carry tenant credentials, tenant usage, private client material, purchases, or billing — the only per-tenant state is marketplace_installs, which is out of this registry's scope (MARKETPLACE-DATA-MODEL.md, §9).

Private Paige artifacts require no external provider. Paige creating a document/image/copy/page/form for a tenant's own private use is a native capability. NATIVE Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 creation (writing into the tenant's own Google/Microsoft account) requires THAT tenant's explicit connected-provider authorization — it is never assumed from a registry listing.

Role/authority is separate from tier. Tier eligibility (who the integration is for) is orthogonal to role/authority (who may act). Admin is a ROLE, never a URL and never a tier (§53/§65). An entry's tier_eligibility never implies any actor may act; that is the authority lane + resolve_tool_autonomy + RLS.

Workers are under Paige's authority, never a bypass. n8n / Zapier / MCP / provider APIs / browser are execution workers governed by the one approval path (§ one-approval-gate); reaching a capability through a different door never grants more permission (door-blindness, governed-execution-seam).

Every consequential external effect owes a canonical provider receipt, a Rail outcome, and a declared cost-track dependency (see cost_tracks). For any effect that moves REAL money — a purchase, payment, ad spend, bookkeeping effect, financial obligation, or other real external spend — the dependency is M1 real-money spend control (§10 reserve/confirm/reconcile/receipt/caps), NEVER satisfied by internal LLM-token metering or estimated cost tracking (owner ruling 2026-09-06). A fired action is not a delivered outcome (§13).

§2 finance is never a platform default. A finance/accounting/credit provider may be an opt-in per-tenant capability but must never be seeded into platform defaults, the coaching-generic registry, or any path that ships to every tenant. Credit is monitoring-only, never repair (§194).

Provider API fees are recorded SEPARATELY from customer money movement (expense_and_operations). Paige Agent AI must not become merchant of record and must not silently charge a tenant's provider account (§38). The expense layer makes operating COST and OWNERSHIP visible; M1 real-money spend control governs external spend AUTHORITY and CAPS. Prices/quotas/terms are mutable — record the official source URL and a checked-as-of date; never invent a price, assume a free plan, or turn an unknown commercial term into a number (§13). Custom/enterprise pricing is recorded honestly as enterprise_contract with no fabricated figure.

delivery_rule.title: The Integration Capability Registry delivery rule (mandatory)
delivery_rule.before: Before proposing, implementing, opening a PR for, or changing ANY provider integration (a third-party API, connector, OAuth scope, Marketplace service, MCP tool over a provider, or external-execution worker), the agent MUST read the relevant registry entry (including its expense_and_operations block) or record that none exists yet.
delivery_rule.on_merge: Before merge, the same PR MUST create or update that entry — capability, authority lane, proof (or PROOF_OWED), limitations, next owner, AND the expense_and_operations block (cost responsibility, billing/operational owner, pricing model + dated source, cost driver, rate limits, renewal/deprecation review, data/privacy/retention, money-movement + M1 real-money-spend-control dependency where applicable, receipt/reconciliation/Rail/pause-revoke) — in the same commit (§0/§66/§BRAIN.3). Shipping the integration change without the registry update is §13/§66 drift.
delivery_rule.enforced_by: docs/brain/README.md index + read-first table, docs/PAIGE-MASTER-PROJECT-REFERENCE.md §3/§4, .claude/skills/second-brain/SKILL.md read table, and the structural guard scripts/ci/integration-registry-lint.mjs (npm run lint:integration-registry).

field_schema.name: human-readable provider/integration name
field_schema.paige_use_cases: concrete things Paige does with it (array)
field_schema.connection_prerequisite: what a tenant/operator must do before it works (OAuth, API key, provider app review, etc.)
field_schema.required_scopes: OAuth scopes / permissions the integration requires (array; names only)
field_schema.safe_readable_context: what Paige may safely read (never raw payload/secrets)
field_schema.allowed_writes_external_effects: the external effects it may cause, and which are gated
field_schema.authority_lane: the highest lane the integration currently supports (array of read/draft/auto/confirm/prohibited)
field_schema.m1_dependency: the cost-track dependency, NAMED per cost_tracks — 'M1 real-money spend control' for spend-capable providers, 'internal LLM-cost metering' for model-usage visibility, or 'none'. Never the unqualified word 'M1' (owner ruling 2026-09-06).
field_schema.canonical_provider_receipt: the provider's own proof an external effect happened (id/receipt), or 'none' if no external effect
field_schema.rail_mind_memory: the Rail (outcome), Mind (eligible knowledge), and Memory (retention) boundaries for this provider
field_schema.status: one of the six status words
field_schema.owner: the workstream that owns this integration
field_schema.dependency: what it depends on to advance
field_schema.marketplace_metadata_only: true only for Platform Marketplace catalogue entries (rule R4 applies)
field_schema.marketplace_package: OPTIONAL. When a provider belongs to a Marketplace package/bundle (e.g. 'Funding & Coaching Tools', owner ruling 2026-09-13), names the package and its governance state. A governance declaration ONLY (R1): naming a package never means it is built, installed, entitled, or available — the package surface and the per-tenant entitlement/connection gate are separate facts recorded honestly in connection_prerequisite + dependency.
field_schema.expense_and_operations: the API Expense & Operations block — see expense_and_operations_schema
field_schema.code_anchors: array of {path, role, note?} objects citing the ACTUAL adapter/entry-point code that backs this provider — a FILE (or a last-segment `*` glob matching files); a bare directory is rejected because directory existence cannot detect file-level drift. REQUIRED and non-empty for runtime-claiming statuses (LIVE/PARTIAL/PROOF_OWED); ABSENT or [] for unbuilt statuses (UNAVAILABLE/DEFERRED/PROPOSED). 'role' is a CONTROLLED, lint-enforced kind (CODE_ANCHOR_ROLES): provider_adapter (the provider's own integration code — API client, send seam, OAuth plumbing, core adapter) | callback_readback (webhook receiver / status callback that reads back the provider's outcome) | fail_closed_containment (a path that deliberately refuses/contains, e.g. a 503) | proven_runtime (ONLY where genuine authenticated end-to-end §32.c runtime proof exists — default DO NOT use; none today). THE HARD RULE (§13): a code anchor proves only that a relevant code PATH EXISTS — NEVER that the provider works, is connected, available, or customer-ready; it NEVER raises status. Every runtime-claiming provider cites at least one PROVIDER-SPECIFIC path; a generic dispatcher/router (model-router, generic send-message, generic mcp-client) is never the sole anchor. Distinct from 'sources' (doc citations). Dead/moved anchors fail CI (lint:integration-registry).

expense_and_operations_schema.note: The API Expense & Operations Layer. Every catalogued provider carries an expense_and_operations block making operating COST and OWNERSHIP visible, SEPARATE from customer money movement (R10/§38). HONESTY STANCE (§13): this is a planning/governance layer — it does NOT verify live vendor prices. Prices/quotas/terms are MUTABLE, so record the OFFICIAL source URL and set pricing_checked_as_of to the date ONLY when a human/next-owner actually verified at that URL; it is null here because this slice did not verify live vendor prices. Never invent a number, never assume a free plan, never turn an unknown commercial term into a number. Custom/enterprise pricing is recorded as enterprise_contract with no fabricated figure.

providers.canonical_provider_receipt: Server-specific authoritative readback/receipt, not a generic successful transport response; production proof owed.
providers.rail_mind_memory: Only sanitized, correlated facts and outcomes; no credential, request header or raw provider payload belongs in Rail, Mind or memory.
providers.dependency: Existing mcp_connections, platform_encrypt/platform_decrypt, canonical RPC writers, mcp-gateway and server-resolved tenant capability checks. No parallel secret store. Authenticated owner save/readback/check and governed execution remain unproven end to end.
